info.title: Janus public read-only API
info.description: The GET routes of the Janus API that take no body and return no personal data: service status, the FAERS snapshot, the séance catalogue, the light-face overview, validation and export, the time machine, the open outcome dataset, the weekly data-quality report, the FAERS onset table of the PIPC rows, the PIPC rows of the open cascade package, the CDS Hooks discovery document and the experimental drug model kit (parameter sets from cited evidence, validation, exports). Medical routes are `no-store`; nothing but an access line (route, status, latency) is logged. Research prototype, not a medical device; not medical advice. Documentation: docs/open-api.md.

rule). An empty `cells` list means that no cell is released yet.

get.description: The released cells as CSV (header only when nothing is released yet).

The current data-quality report: findings with their class and status against the
previous run, the sources and the rules. Codes and counts only.
All 65 PIPC rows with their FAERS report counts and reported time to onset.
One PIPC row (1-65) with the dataset's caveats.

The 65 PIPC rows (CC BY 4.0) with Janus's class mapping (Apache-2.0), package version and
citation. Published data only; no personal data.
CDS Hooks discovery: the `janus-cascade` service for `order-select` and `order-sign`.

The drugs of the experimental model kit with their validation status. `q` keeps the drugs
whose name contains it, `status` and `has_set` filter; `limit` (at most 200) and `offset` page
the answer. Sorted by name.
One drug: parameter set, validation report and what was left out.
Every evidence row of the drug with its quote, source and both reader verdicts.
A zip with the model file(s), provenance.json, references.bib and LICENSES.txt.
The system report over all drugs: counts by status, pooled fold errors with n.

Split-conformal interval of one metric over the held-out studies of the release. `fold_half` is the
factor by which the prediction is divided and multiplied (coverage `coverage` of new studies); None
when it is not shown (`reason` says why).
